angularDiameterSource: Stellar radius 0.411 ± 0.038 solar radii from Sarkis et al. (2018), AJ 155, 257, Table 2. It is a radius from stellar characterisation, not an interferometric diameter; the angular diameter in the record is that radius at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia EDR3 parallax 26.2469 +/- 0.0266 mas via SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G): 1000/26.2469 = 38.10 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: 0.411 +/- 0.038 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius, the stellar radius in Sarkis et al. (2018, AJ 155, 257; arXiv:1805.00830, Table 2). GM from their stellar mass 0.359 +/- 0.047 solar masses times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. presentationUp: no spin axis is measured, so the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; no picture of the photosphere is cast.
